newsitem.title: GERMANY: Cartel plea mulled in German bourse dispute.
newsitem.headline: Cartel plea mulled in German bourse dispute.

text.p: Four regional German stock exchanges on Tuesday said they were considering an appeal to cartel authorities in a continuing dispute over possible nationwide co-operation with their larger rivals.

The four bourses in Stuttgart, Bremen, Hamburg and Hanover have been negotiating to join a co-operation pact that already links the stock exchanges in Frankfurt, Berlin, Munich and Dusseldorf, but the talks are taking on a combative tone.

In a joint statement Tuesday afternoon, the exchanges claimed that their application to link with the larger bourses had been turned down, a claim which Deutsche Boerse AG, the umbrella group for Germany's exchange system, has denied.
Dirk Hoffmann, head of the Hanover bourse, said the small exchanges were mulling an approach to the cartel office to ensure their competitive positions were not in danger.
The dispute pivots on an agreement which forms part of the pact between Frankfurt, Berlin, Munich and Dusseldorf and is aimed at harmonising pricing systems at the four centres.

Deutsche Boerse, which is known to be keen for more harmonisation between the exchanges, wants the four prospective newcomers to take part in this pricing system on a gradual basis, but not immediately.
"We did not reject their application. On the contrary, we offered the bourses a gradual entry to the cooperation pact," a spokesman for Deutsche Boerse told Reuters.

Traditionally, German's four smallest bourses have been reluctant to consider a nationwide cooperation, fearing a loss of business and influence under the shadow of the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, the undisputed market leader.
Two years ago the regional bourses agreed a comprehensive cooperation proposal for the first time, but differences of opinion meant the proposal was never approved.
